metric.label: Lexical baseline
metric.description: Character n-gram cosine distance. This is a reproducible lexical baseline, not a semantic or faithfulness score.

units.leftText: This is the word of the LORD that came to Micah the Moreshite in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah — what he saw regarding Samaria and Jerusalem:
units.rightText: The word of Jehovah that came to Micah the Morashtite in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, which he saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem.

units.leftText: Hear, O peoples, all of you; listen, O earth, and everyone in it! May the Lord GOD bear witness against you, the Lord from His holy temple.
units.rightText: Hear, ye peoples, all of you; hearken, O earth, and all that therein is: and let the Lord Jehovah be witness against you, the Lord from his holy temple.

units.leftText: For behold, the LORD comes forth from His dwelling place; He will come down and tread on the high places of the earth.
units.rightText: For, behold, Jehovah cometh forth out of his place, and will come down, and tread upon the high places of the earth.

units.leftText: The mountains will melt beneath Him, and the valleys will split apart, like wax before the fire, like water rushing down a slope.
units.rightText: And the mountains shall be melted under him, and the valleys shall be cleft, as wax before the fire, as waters that are poured down a steep place.

units.leftText: All this is for the transgression of Jacob and the sins of the house of Israel. What is the transgression of Jacob? Is it not Samaria? And what is the high place of Judah? Is it not Jerusalem?
units.rightText: For the transgression of Jacob is all this, and for the sins of the house of Israel. What is the transgression of Jacob? is it not Samaria? and what are the high places of Judah? are they not Jerusalem?

units.leftText: Therefore I will make Samaria a heap of rubble in the open field, a planting area for a vineyard. I will pour her stones into the valley and expose her foundations.
units.rightText: Therefore I will make Samaria as a heap of the field, and as places for planting vineyards; and I will pour down the stones thereof into the valley, and I will uncover the foundations thereof.

units.leftText: All her carved images will be smashed to pieces; all her wages will be burned in the fire, and I will destroy all her idols. Since she collected the wages of a prostitute, they will be used again on a prostitute. Weeping and Mourning
units.rightText: And all her graven images shall be beaten to pieces, and all her hires shall be burned with fire, and all her idols will I lay desolate; for of the hire of a harlot hath she gathered them, and unto the hire of a harlot shall they return.

units.leftText: Because of this I will lament and wail; I will walk barefoot and naked. I will howl like a jackal and mourn like an ostrich.
units.rightText: For this will I lament and wail; I will go stripped and naked; I will make a wailing like the jackals, and a lamentation like the ostriches.
leftNotes: 1:8 Or a serpent or a dragon
1:8 Literally like daughters of an ostrich or like daughters of an owl

units.leftText: For her wound is incurable; it has reached even Judah; it has approached the gate of my people, as far as Jerusalem itself.
units.rightText: For her wounds are incurable; for it is come even unto Judah; it reacheth unto the gate of my people, even to Jerusalem.

units.leftText: Do not tell it in Gath; do not weep at all. Roll in the dust in Beth-leaphrah.
units.rightText: Tell it not in Gath, weep not at all: at Beth-le-aphrah have I rolled myself in the dust.
leftNotes: 1:10 Gath sounds like the Hebrew for tell.
1:10 Beth-leaphrah means house of dust.

units.leftText: Depart in shameful nakedness, O dwellers of Shaphir. The dwellers of Zaanan will not come out. Beth-ezel is in mourning; its support is taken from you.
units.rightText: Pass away, O inhabitant of Shaphir, in nakedness and shame: the inhabitant of Zaanan is not come forth; the wailing of Beth-ezel shall take from you the stay thereof.
leftNotes: 1:11 Shaphir means pleasant.
1:11 Zaanan sounds like the Hebrew for come out.
1:11 Beth-ezel means adjoining house.

units.leftText: For the dwellers of Maroth pined for good, but calamity came down from the LORD, even to the gate of Jerusalem.
units.rightText: For the inhabitant of Maroth waiteth anxiously for good, because evil is come down from Jehovah unto the gate of Jerusalem.
leftNotes: 1:12 Maroth sounds like the Hebrew for bitter.

units.leftText: Harness your chariot horses, O dweller of Lachish. You were the beginning of sin to the Daughter of Zion, for the transgressions of Israel were found in you.
units.rightText: Bind the chariot to the swift steed, O inhabitant of Lachish: she was the beginning of sin to the daughter of Zion; for the transgressions of Israel were found in thee.
leftNotes: 1:13 Lachish sounds like the Hebrew term for team of horses.

units.leftText: Therefore, send farewell gifts to Moresheth-gath; the houses of Achzib will prove deceptive to the kings of Israel.
units.rightText: Therefore shalt thou give a parting gift to Moresheth-gath: the houses of Achzib shall be a deceitful thing unto the kings of Israel.
leftNotes: 1:14 Or give dowry
1:14 Moresheth sounds like the Hebrew for gift or dowry.
1:14 Achzib means deception.

units.leftText: I will again bring a conqueror against you, O dweller of Mareshah. The glory of Israel will come to Adullam.
units.rightText: I will yet bring unto thee, O inhabitant of Mareshah, him that shall possess thee: the glory of Israel shall come even unto Adullam.
leftNotes: 1:15 Mareshah sounds like the Hebrew for conqueror.

units.leftText: Shave yourselves bald and cut off your hair in mourning for your precious children; make yourselves as bald as an eagle, for they will go from you into exile.
units.rightText: Make thee bald, and cut off thy hair for the children of thy delight: enlarge thy baldness as the eagle; for they are gone into captivity from thee.

units.leftText: Woe to those who devise iniquity and plot evil on their beds! At morning’s light they accomplish it because the power is in their hands.
units.rightText: Woe to them that devise iniquity and work evil upon their beds! when the morning is light, they practise it, because it is in the power of their hand.

units.leftText: They covet fields and seize them; they take away houses. They deprive a man of his home, a fellow man of his inheritance.
units.rightText: And they covet fields, and seize them; and houses, and take them away: and they oppress a man and his house, even a man and his heritage.

units.leftText: Therefore this is what the LORD says: “I am planning against this nation a disaster from which you cannot free your necks. Then you will not walk so proudly, for it will be a time of calamity.
units.rightText: Therefore thus saith Jehovah: Behold, against this family do I devise an evil, from which ye shall not remove your necks, neither shall ye walk haughtily; for it is an evil time.

units.leftText: In that day they will take up a proverb against you and taunt you with this bitter lamentation: ‘We are utterly ruined! He has changed the portion of my people. How He has removed it from me! He has allotted our fields to traitors.’”
units.rightText: In that day shall they take up a parable against you, and lament with a doleful lamentation, and say, We are utterly ruined: he changeth the portion of my people: how doth he remove it from me! to the rebellious he divideth our fields.

units.leftText: Therefore, you will have no one in the assembly of the LORD to divide the land by lot. Reproof of False Prophets (Ezekiel 13:1–16|EZK 13:1-16*)
units.rightText: Therefore thou shalt have none that shall cast the line by lot in the assembly of Jehovah.

units.leftText: “Do not preach,” they preach. “Do not preach these things; disgrace will not overtake us.”
units.rightText: Prophesy ye not, thus they prophesy. They shall not prophesy to these: reproaches shall not depart.

units.leftText: Should it be said, O house of Jacob, “Is the Spirit of the LORD impatient? Are these the things He does?” Do not My words bring good to him who walks uprightly?
units.rightText: Shall it be said, O house of Jacob, Is the Spirit of Jehovah straitened? are these his doings? Do not my words do good to him that walketh uprightly?

units.leftText: But of late My people have risen up like an enemy: You strip off the splendid robe from unsuspecting passersby like men returning from battle.
units.rightText: But of late my people is risen up as an enemy: ye strip the robe from off the garment from them that pass by securely as men averse from war.

units.leftText: You drive the women of My people from their pleasant homes. You take away My blessing from their children forever.
units.rightText: The women of my people ye cast out from their pleasant houses; from their young children ye take away my glory for ever.

units.leftText: Arise and depart, for this is not your place of rest, because its defilement brings destruction— a grievous destruction!
units.rightText: Arise ye, and depart; for this is not your resting-place; because of uncleanness that destroyeth, even with a grievous destruction.

units.leftText: If a man of wind were to come and say falsely, “I will preach to you of wine and strong drink,” he would be just the preacher for this people! The Remnant of Israel (Micah 5:7–15|MIC 5:7-15*)
units.rightText: If a man walking in a spirit of falsehood do lie, saying, I will prophesy unto thee of wine and of strong drink; he shall even be the prophet of this people.
leftNotes: 2:11 Or “I will prophesy to you for wine and strong drink”

units.leftText: I will surely gather all of you, O Jacob; I will collect the remnant of Israel. I will bring them together like sheep in a pen, like a flock in the midst of its pasture — a noisy throng.
units.rightText: I will surely assemble, O Jacob, all of thee; I will surely gather the remnant of Israel; I will put them together as the sheep of Bozrah, as a flock in the midst of their pasture; they shall make great noise by reason of the multitude of men.

units.leftText: One who breaks open the way will go up before them; they will break through the gate, and go out by it. Their King will pass through before them, the LORD as their leader.
units.rightText: The breaker is gone up before them: they have broken forth and passed on to the gate, and are gone out thereat; and their king is passed on before them, and Jehovah at the head of them.

units.leftText: Then I said: “Hear now, O leaders of Jacob, you rulers of the house of Israel. Should you not know justice?
units.rightText: And I said, Hear, I pray you, ye heads of Jacob, and rulers of the house of Israel: is it not for you to know justice?

units.leftText: You hate good and love evil. You tear the skin from my people and strip the flesh from their bones.
units.rightText: ye who hate the good, and love the evil; who pluck off their skin from off them, and their flesh from off their bones;

units.leftText: You eat the flesh of my people after stripping off their skin and breaking their bones. You chop them up like flesh for the cooking pot, like meat in a cauldron.”
units.rightText: who also eat the flesh of my people, and flay their skin from off them, and break their bones, and chop them in pieces, as for the pot, and as flesh within the caldron.

units.leftText: Then they will cry out to the LORD, but He will not answer them. At that time He will hide His face from them because of the evil they have done.
units.rightText: Then shall they cry unto Jehovah, but he will not answer them; yea, he will hide his face from them at that time, according as they have wrought evil in their doings.

units.leftText: This is what the LORD says: “As for the prophets who lead My people astray, who proclaim peace while they chew with their teeth, but declare war against one who puts nothing in their mouths:
units.rightText: Thus saith Jehovah concerning the prophets that make my people to err; that bite with their teeth, and cry, Peace; and whoso putteth not into their mouths, they even prepare war against him:

units.leftText: Therefore night will come over you without visions, and darkness without divination. The sun will set on these prophets, and the daylight will turn black over them.
units.rightText: Therefore it shall be night unto you, that ye shall have no vision; and it shall be dark unto you, that ye shall not divine; and the sun shall go down upon the prophets, and the day shall be black over them.

units.leftText: Then the seers will be ashamed and the diviners will be disgraced. They will all cover their mouths because there is no answer from God.”
units.rightText: And the seers shall be put to shame, and the diviners confounded; yea, they shall all cover their lips; for there is no answer of God.

units.leftText: As for me, however, I am filled with power by the Spirit of the LORD, with justice and courage, to declare to Jacob his transgression and to Israel his sin.
units.rightText: But as for me, I am full of power by the Spirit of Jehovah, and of judgment, and of might, to declare unto Jacob his transgression, and to Israel his sin.

units.leftText: Now hear this, O leaders of the house of Jacob and rulers of the house of Israel, who despise justice and pervert all that is right,
units.rightText: Hear this, I pray you, ye heads of the house of Jacob, and rulers of the house of Israel, that abhor justice, and pervert all equity.

units.leftText: who build Zion with bloodshed and Jerusalem with iniquity.
units.rightText: They build up Zion with blood, and Jerusalem with iniquity.

units.leftText: Her leaders judge for a bribe, her priests teach for a price, and her prophets practice divination for money. Yet they lean upon the LORD, saying, “Is not the LORD among us? No disaster can come upon us.”
units.rightText: The heads thereof judge for reward, and the priests thereof teach for hire, and the prophets thereof divine for money: yet they lean upon Jehovah, and say, Is not Jehovah in the midst of us? no evil shall come upon us.

units.leftText: Therefore, because of you, Zion will be plowed like a field, Jerusalem will become a heap of rubble, and the temple mount a wooded ridge.
units.rightText: Therefore shall Zion for your sake be plowed as a field, and Jerusalem shall become heaps, and the mountain of the house as the high places of a forest.

units.leftText: In the last days the mountain of the house of the LORD will be established as the chief of the mountains; it will be raised above the hills, and the peoples will stream to it.
units.rightText: But in the latter days it shall come to pass, that the mountain of Jehovah’s house shall be established on the top of the mountains, and it shall be exalted above the hills; and peoples shall flow unto it.

units.leftText: And many nations will come and say: “Come, let us go up to the mountain of the LORD, to the house of the God of Jacob. He will teach us His ways, so that we may walk in His paths.” For the law will go forth from Zion and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem.
units.rightText: And many nations shall go and say, Come ye, and let us go up to the mountain of Jehovah, and to the house of the God of Jacob; and he will teach us of his ways, and we will walk in his paths. For out of Zion shall go forth the law, and the word of Jehovah from Jerusalem;

units.leftText: Then He will judge between many peoples and arbitrate for strong nations far and wide. Then they will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks. Nation will no longer take up the sword against nation, nor will they train anymore for war.
units.rightText: and he will judge between many peoples, and will decide concerning strong nations afar off: and they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruning-hooks; nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more.

units.leftText: And each man will sit under his own vine and under his own fig tree, with no one to frighten him. For the mouth of the LORD of Hosts has spoken.
units.rightText: But they shall sit every man under his vine and under his fig-tree; and none shall make them afraid: for the mouth of Jehovah of hosts hath spoken it.

units.leftText: Though all the nations may walk in the name of their gods, yet we will walk in the name of the LORD our God forever and ever. The Restoration of Zion (Zechariah 8:1–23|ZEC 8:1-23*)
units.rightText: For all the peoples walk every one in the name of his god; and we will walk in the name of Jehovah our God for ever and ever.

units.leftText: “On that day,” declares the LORD, “I will gather the lame; I will assemble the outcast, even those whom I have afflicted.
units.rightText: In that day, saith Jehovah, will I assemble that which is lame, and I will gather that which is driven away, and that which I have afflicted;

units.leftText: And I will make the lame into a remnant, the outcast into a strong nation. Then the LORD will rule over them in Mount Zion from that day and forever.
units.rightText: and I will make that which was lame a remnant, and that which was cast far off a strong nation: and Jehovah will reign over them in mount Zion from henceforth even for ever.

units.leftText: And you, O watchtower of the flock, O stronghold of the Daughter of Zion — the former dominion will be restored to you; sovereignty will come to the Daughter of Jerusalem.”
units.rightText: And thou, O tower of the flock, the hill of the daughter of Zion, unto thee shall it come, yea, the former dominion shall come, the kingdom of the daughter of Jerusalem.
leftNotes: 4:8 Or hill; Hebrew And you, Migdal-eder, the Ophel

units.leftText: Why do you now cry aloud? Is there no king among you? Has your counselor perished so that anguish grips you like a woman in labor?
units.rightText: Now why dost thou cry out aloud? Is there no king in thee, is thy counsellor perished, that pangs have taken hold of thee as of a woman in travail?

units.leftText: Writhe in agony, O Daughter of Zion, like a woman in labor. For now you will leave the city and camp in the open fields. You will go to Babylon; there you will be rescued; there the LORD will redeem you from the hand of your enemies!
units.rightText: Be in pain, and labor to bring forth, O daughter of Zion, like a woman in travail; for now shalt thou go forth out of the city, and shalt dwell in the field, and shalt come even unto Babylon: there shalt thou be rescued; there will Jehovah redeem thee from the hand of thine enemies.

units.leftText: But now many nations have assembled against you, saying, “Let her be defiled, and let us feast our eyes on Zion.”
units.rightText: And now many nations are assembled against thee, that say, Let her be defiled, and let our eye see our desire upon Zion.

units.leftText: But they do not know the thoughts of the LORD or understand His plan, for He has gathered them like sheaves to the threshing floor.
units.rightText: But they know not the thoughts of Jehovah, neither understand they his counsel; for he hath gathered them as the sheaves to the threshing-floor.

units.leftText: Rise and thresh, O Daughter of Zion, for I will give you horns of iron and hooves of bronze to break to pieces many peoples. Then you will devote their gain to the LORD, their wealth to the Lord of all the earth.
units.rightText: Arise and thresh, O daughter of Zion; for I will make thy horn iron, and I will make thy hoofs brass; and thou shalt beat in pieces many peoples: and I will devote their gain unto Jehovah, and their substance unto the Lord of the whole earth.
leftNotes: 4:13 Or devote to destruction

units.leftText: Now, O daughter of troops, mobilize your troops; for a siege is laid against us! With a rod they will strike the cheek of the judge of Israel.
units.rightText: Now shalt thou gather thyself in troops, O daughter of troops: he hath laid siege against us; they shall smite the judge of Israel with a rod upon the cheek.

units.leftText: But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, who are small among the clans of Judah, out of you will come forth for Me One to be ruler over Israel — One whose origins are of old, from the days of eternity.
units.rightText: But thou, Beth-lehem Ephrathah, which art little to be among the thousands of Judah, out of thee shall one come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel; whose goings forth are from of old, from everlasting.
leftNotes: 5:2 Or thousands
5:2 Cited in Matthew 2:6|MAT 2:6*

units.leftText: Therefore Israel will be abandoned until she who is in labor has given birth; then the rest of His brothers will return to the children of Israel.
units.rightText: Therefore will he give them up, until the time that she who travaileth hath brought forth: then the residue of his brethren shall return unto the children of Israel.

units.leftText: He will stand and shepherd His flock in the strength of the LORD, in the majestic name of the LORD His God. And they will dwell securely, for then His greatness will extend to the ends of the earth.
units.rightText: And he shall stand, and shall feed his flock in the strength of Jehovah, in the majesty of the name of Jehovah his God: and they shall abide; for now shall he be great unto the ends of the earth.

units.leftText: And He will be our peace when Assyria invades our land and tramples our citadels. We will raise against it seven shepherds, even eight leaders of men.
units.rightText: And this man shall be our peace. When the Assyrian shall come into our land, and when he shall tread in our palaces, then shall we raise against him seven shepherds, and eight principal men.
leftNotes: 5:5 Or their peace

units.leftText: And they will rule the land of Assyria with the sword, and the land of Nimrod with the blade drawn. So He will deliver us when Assyria invades our land and marches into our borders. The Remnant of Jacob (Micah 2:12–13|MIC 2:12-13*)
units.rightText: And they shall waste the land of Assyria with the sword, and the land of Nimrod in the entrances thereof: and he shall deliver us from the Assyrian, when he cometh into our land, and when he treadeth within our border.

units.leftText: Then the remnant of Jacob will be in the midst of many peoples like dew from the LORD, like showers on the grass, which do not wait for man or linger for mankind.
units.rightText: And the remnant of Jacob shall be in the midst of many peoples as dew from Jehovah, as showers upon the grass, that tarry not for man, nor wait for the sons of men.

units.leftText: Then the remnant of Jacob will be among the nations, in the midst of many peoples, like a lion among the beasts of the forest, like a young lion among flocks of sheep, which tramples and tears as it passes through, with no one to rescue them.
units.rightText: And the remnant of Jacob shall be among the nations, in the midst of many peoples, as a lion among the beasts of the forest, as a young lion among the flocks of sheep; who, if he go through, treadeth down and teareth in pieces, and there is none to deliver.

units.leftText: Your hand will be lifted over your foes, and all your enemies will be cut off.
units.rightText: Let thy hand be lifted up above thine adversaries, and let all thine enemies be cut off.

units.leftText: “In that day,” declares the LORD, “I will remove your horses from among you and wreck your chariots.
units.rightText: And it shall come to pass in that day, saith Jehovah, that I will cut off thy horses out of the midst of thee, and will destroy thy chariots:

units.leftText: I will remove the cities of your land and tear down all your strongholds.
units.rightText: and I will cut off the cities of thy land, and will throw down all thy strongholds.

units.leftText: I will cut the sorceries from your hand, and you will have no fortune-tellers.
units.rightText: And I will cut off witchcrafts out of thy hand; and thou shalt have no more soothsayers:

units.leftText: I will also cut off the carved images and sacred pillars from among you, so that you will no longer bow down to the work of your own hands.
units.rightText: and I will cut off thy graven images and thy pillars out of the midst of thee; and thou shalt no more worship the work of thy hands;

units.leftText: I will root out the Asherah poles from your midst and demolish your cities.
units.rightText: and I will pluck up thine Asherim out of the midst of thee; and I will destroy thy cities.

units.leftText: I will take vengeance in anger and wrath upon the nations that have not obeyed Me.”
units.rightText: And I will execute vengeance in anger and wrath upon the nations which hearkened not.

units.leftText: Hear now what the LORD says: “Arise, plead your case before the mountains, and let the hills hear your voice.
units.rightText: Hear ye now what Jehovah saith: Arise, contend thou before the mountains, and let the hills hear thy voice.

units.leftText: Hear, O mountains, the LORD’s indictment, you enduring foundations of the earth. For the LORD has a case against His people, and He will argue it against Israel:
units.rightText: Hear, O ye mountains, Jehovah’s controversy, and ye enduring foundations of the earth; for Jehovah hath a controversy with his people, and he will contend with Israel.

units.leftText: ‘My people, what have I done to you? Testify against Me how I have wearied you!
units.rightText: O my people, what have I done unto thee? and wherein have I wearied thee? testify against me.

units.leftText: For I brought you up from the land of Egypt and redeemed you from the house of slavery. I sent Moses before you, as well as Aaron and Miriam.
units.rightText: For I brought thee up out of the land of Egypt, and redeemed thee out of the house of bondage; and I sent before thee Moses, Aaron, and Miriam.

units.leftText: My people, remember what Balak king of Moab counseled and what Balaam son of Beor answered. Remember your journey from Shittim to Gilgal, so that you may acknowledge the righteousness of the LORD.’”
units.rightText: O my people, remember now what Balak king of Moab devised, and what Balaam the son of Beor answered him; remember from Shittim unto Gilgal, that ye may know the righteous acts of Jehovah.
leftNotes: 6:5 Or Acacia Grove

units.leftText: With what shall I come before the LORD when I bow before the God on high? Should I come to Him with burnt offerings, with year-old calves?
units.rightText: Wherewith shall I come before Jehovah, and bow myself before the high God? shall I come before him with burnt-offerings, with calves a year old?

units.leftText: Would the LORD be pleased with thousands of rams, with ten thousand rivers of oil? Shall I present my firstborn for my transgression, the fruit of my body for the sin of my soul?
units.rightText: will Jehovah be pleased with thousands of rams, or with ten thousands of rivers of oil? shall I give my first-born for my transgression, the fruit of my body for the sin of my soul?

units.leftText: He has shown you, O man, what is good. And what does the LORD require of you but to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God? The Punishment of Israel
units.rightText: He hath showed thee, O man, what is good; and what doth Jehovah require of thee, but to do justly, and to love kindness, and to walk humbly with thy God?

units.leftText: The voice of the LORD calls out to the city (and it is sound wisdom to fear Your name): “Heed the rod and the One who ordained it.
units.rightText: The voice of Jehovah crieth unto the city, and the man of wisdom will see thy name: hear ye the rod, and who hath appointed it.

units.leftText: Can I forget any longer, O house of the wicked, the treasures of wickedness and the short ephah, which is accursed?
units.rightText: Are there yet treasures of wickedness in the house of the wicked, and a scant measure that is abominable?

units.leftText: Can I excuse dishonest scales or bags of false weights?
units.rightText: Shall I be pure with wicked balances, and with a bag of deceitful weights?

units.leftText: For the wealthy of the city are full of violence, and its residents speak lies; their tongues are deceitful in their mouths.
units.rightText: For the rich men thereof are full of violence, and the inhabitants thereof have spoken lies, and their tongue is deceitful in their mouth.

units.leftText: Therefore I am striking you severely, to ruin you because of your sins.
units.rightText: Therefore I also have smitten thee with a grievous wound; I have made thee desolate because of thy sins.

units.leftText: You will eat but not be satisfied, and your hunger will remain with you. What you acquire, you will not preserve; and what you save, I will give to the sword.
units.rightText: Thou shalt eat, but not be satisfied; and thy humiliation shall be in the midst of thee: and thou shalt put away, but shalt not save; and that which thou savest will I give up to the sword.

units.leftText: You will sow but not reap; you will press olives but not anoint yourselves with oil; you will tread grapes but not drink the wine.
units.rightText: Thou shalt sow, but shalt not reap; thou shalt tread the olives, but shalt not anoint thee with oil; and the vintage, but shalt not drink the wine.

units.leftText: You have kept the statutes of Omri and all the practices of Ahab’s house; you have followed their counsel. Therefore I will make you a desolation, and your inhabitants an object of contempt; you will bear the scorn of the nations. ”
units.rightText: For the statutes of Omri are kept, and all the works of the house of Ahab, and ye walk in their counsels; that I may make thee a desolation, and the inhabitants thereof a hissing: and ye shall bear the reproach of my people.
leftNotes: 6:16 LXX; Hebrew scorn of My people

units.leftText: Woe is me! For I am like one gathering summer fruit at the gleaning of the vineyard; there is no cluster to eat, no early fig that I crave.
units.rightText: Woe is me! for I am as when they have gathered the summer fruits, as the grape gleanings of the vintage: there is no cluster to eat; my soul desireth the first-ripe fig.

units.leftText: The godly man has perished from the earth; there is no one upright among men. They all lie in wait for blood; they hunt one another with a net.
units.rightText: The godly man is perished out of the earth, and there is none upright among men: they all lie in wait for blood; they hunt every man his brother with a net.

units.leftText: Both hands are skilled at evil; the prince and the judge demand a bribe. When the powerful utters his evil desire, they all conspire together.
units.rightText: Their hands are upon that which is evil to do it diligently; the prince asketh, and the judge is ready for a reward; and the great man, he uttereth the evil desire of his soul: thus they weave it together.

units.leftText: The best of them is like a brier; the most upright is sharper than a hedge of thorns. The day for your watchmen has come, the day of your visitation. Now is the time of their confusion.
units.rightText: The best of them is as a brier; the most upright is worse than a thorn hedge: the day of thy watchmen, even thy visitation, is come; now shall be their perplexity.
leftNotes: 7:4 Or your punishment

units.leftText: Do not rely on a friend; do not trust in a companion. Seal the doors of your mouth from her who lies in your arms.
units.rightText: Trust ye not in a neighbor; put ye not confidence in a friend; keep the doors of thy mouth from her that lieth in thy bosom.
leftNotes: 7:5 Hebrew in your bosom

units.leftText: For a son dishonors his father, a daughter rises against her mother, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law. A man’s enemies are the members of his own household. Israel’s Confession and Comfort
units.rightText: For the son dishonoreth the father, the daughter riseth up against her mother, the daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law; a man’s enemies are the men of his own house.
leftNotes: 7:6 Cited in Matthew 10:35–36|MAT 10:35-36*; see also Luke 12:53.

units.leftText: But as for me, I will look to the LORD; I will wait for the God of my salvation. My God will hear me.
units.rightText: But as for me, I will look unto Jehovah; I will wait for the God of my salvation: my God will hear me.

units.leftText: Do not gloat over me, my enemy! Though I have fallen, I will arise; though I sit in darkness, the LORD will be my light.
units.rightText: Rejoice not against me, O mine enemy: when I fall, I shall arise; when I sit in darkness, Jehovah will be a light unto me.

units.leftText: Because I have sinned against Him, I must endure the rage of the LORD, until He argues my case and executes justice for me. He will bring me into the light; I will see His righteousness.
units.rightText: I will bear the indignation of Jehovah, because I have sinned against him, until he plead my cause, and execute judgment for me: he will bring me forth to the light, and I shall behold his righteousness.

units.leftText: Then my enemy will see and will be covered with shame — she who said to me, “Where is the LORD your God?” My eyes will see her; at that time she will be trampled like mud in the streets.
units.rightText: Then mine enemy shall see it, and shame shall cover her who said unto me, Where is Jehovah thy God? Mine eyes shall see my desire upon her; now shall she be trodden down as the mire of the streets.

units.leftText: The day for rebuilding your walls will come — the day for extending your boundary.
units.rightText: A day for building thy walls! in that day shall the decree be far removed.

units.leftText: On that day they will come to you from Assyria and the cities of Egypt, even from Egypt to the Euphrates, from sea to sea and mountain to mountain.
units.rightText: In that day shall they come unto thee from Assyria and the cities of Egypt, and from Egypt even to the River, and from sea to sea, and from mountain to mountain.
leftNotes: 7:12 Hebrew the River

units.leftText: Then the earth will become desolate because of its inhabitants, as the fruit of their deeds. God’s Compassion on Israel
units.rightText: Yet shall the land be desolate because of them that dwell therein, for the fruit of their doings.

units.leftText: Shepherd with Your staff Your people, the flock of Your inheritance. They live alone in a woodland, surrounded by pastures. Let them graze in Bashan and Gilead, as in the days of old.
units.rightText: Feed thy people with thy rod, the flock of thy heritage, which dwell solitarily, in the forest in the midst of Carmel: let them feed in Bashan and Gilead, as in the days of old.
leftNotes: 7:14 Or in a woodland, in the midst of Carmel

units.leftText: As in the days when you came out of Egypt, I will show My wonders.
units.rightText: As in the days of thy coming forth out of the land of Egypt will I show unto them marvellous things.

units.leftText: Nations will see and be ashamed, deprived of all their might. They will put their hands over their mouths, and their ears will become deaf.
units.rightText: The nations shall see and be ashamed of all their might; they shall lay their hand upon their mouth; their ears shall be deaf.

units.leftText: They will lick the dust like a snake, like reptiles slithering on the ground. They will come trembling from their strongholds in the presence of the LORD our God; they will tremble in fear of You.
units.rightText: They shall lick the dust like a serpent; like crawling things of the earth they shall come trembling out of their close places; they shall come with fear unto Jehovah our God, and shall be afraid because of thee.

units.leftText: Who is a God like You, who pardons iniquity and passes over the transgression of the remnant of His inheritance — who does not retain His anger forever, because He delights in loving devotion?
units.rightText: Who is a God like unto thee, that pardoneth iniquity, and passeth over the transgression of the remnant of his heritage? he retaineth not his anger for ever, because he delighteth in lovingkindness.
leftNotes: 7:18 Forms of the Hebrew chesed are translated here and in most cases throughout the Scriptures as loving devotion; the range of meaning includes love, goodness, kindness, faithfulness, and mercy, as well as loyalty to a covenant.

units.leftText: He will again have compassion on us; He will vanquish our iniquities. You will cast out all our sins into the depths of the sea.
units.rightText: He will again have compassion upon us; he will tread our iniquities under foot; and thou wilt cast all their sins into the depths of the sea.

units.leftText: You will show faithfulness to Jacob and loving devotion to Abraham, as You swore to our fathers from the days of old.
units.rightText: Thou wilt perform the truth to Jacob, and the lovingkindness to Abraham, which thou hast sworn unto our fathers from the days of old.
